newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedbank in coop with Sparebank1Gruppen.
newsitem.headline: Swedbank in coop with Sparebank1Gruppen.

text.p: Swedish bank Swedbank said on Monday it was stepping up cooperation with Norway's SpareBank1Gruppen on fund and insurance products for the Norwegian private market.

"As a first step in the development of this future cooperation, Swedbank has received options to acquire in two stages up to 50 percent of shares in SpareBank1Gruppen's subsidiary Odin Forvaltning AS by the end of 1999," Swedbank said in a statement.
Odin's activities include unit trust and interest fund business in the Norwegian market, it said. At the end of 1996 the company had an investment capital of around four billion Norwegian crowns.
On the insurance side, Swedbank and SpareBank1Gruppen have agreed to develop activities together on an equal basis, Swedbank said.

Swedbank has options to buy 10 percent of shares in SpareBank1Gruppen's subsidiary, Sparebank1 Livforsikring AS former DAVID Forsikring AS, and 90 percent of the shares in the unit linked company, Sparbank1 Unit Linked which the SpareBank1Gruppen is in the process of forming.
The SpareBank1Gruppen has a customer base of more than one million customers and around 35 percent of the Norwegian savings bank market, Swedbank said.
Swedbank also plans to undertake options of up to 9.8 percent in Norway's Fokus Bank.

"The major part of these shares have already been acquired by Swedbank. The SpareBank1Gruppen has then in turn the right to acquire these options, or, in the framework of the public offer made by the SpareBank1Gruppen for the shares in Fokus, the shares that the options relate to," it said.
SpareBank1Gruppen placed a bid on Fokus Bank earlier this year.
